title: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule
text:
Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule

['From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>\\nTo: Jacob Lee <jacob@clearwellhealth.com>\\nCc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>\\nDate: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule\\n\\nHi Jacob / Emma —\\n\\nThanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks I promised to follow up on:\\n\\n- Recap: ClearWell is evaluating options for inference hosting: Hosted API for initial rollout vs Reserved Dedicated capacity for consistent throughput vs Private VPC for regulated PHI use.\\n- Primary concerns you raised: noisy-neighbor risk under bursty workloads, isolation boundaries for KV caches and model artifacts, and meeting 99.9% token-level latency SLOs.\\n\\nWhat I attached: a short \\"redwood-tenancy-playbook.pdf\\" with examples of isolation controls and operational evidence, and a sample SLO table (poa_slo_table.xlsx) that maps workloads -> recommended mode.\\n\\nImmediate next steps I propose:\\n1) I’ll share the playbook (attached) with the technical touches we discussed.\\n2) Vanessa can provide short, concrete examples of historical noisy-neighbor incidents and how we mitigated them.\\n3) If you’re comfortable, we can scope a 2-week POC (Dedicated pool with VPC peering) — propose kickoff week of July 12.\\n\\nQuestions for you to confirm:\\n- Is PHI expected in inference payloads during the POC, or only sanitized data?\\n- Target SLO (p95/p99) you need for the first milestone?\\n\\nHappy to jump on another quick call to walk through the playbook.\\n\\nBest,\\nMichael Grant\\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\\nmichael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182\\n\\nAttachments: redwood-tenancy-playbook.pdf (12 pages, diagram + examples)\\n', 'From: Jacob Lee <jacob@clearwellhealth.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>\\nCc: Emma Torres <emma.torres@clearwellhealth.com>\\nDate: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule\\n\\nThanks Michael — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: \\n\\n- PHI: for the initial POC we will only use de-identified records; downstream we will almost certainly need a PHI flow.\\n- SLOs: our first target is p95 latency < 220ms, p99 < 550ms for 1–2k qps. If Dedicated can show consistent p99 under load, that’s a big plus.\\n- Noisy neighbor example: can you share a real incident timeline (not just high-level), i.e., a past case where we saw tail latency spikes, root cause, how long it took to mitigate, and what the fallback looked like?\\n\\nAlso, we need to loop in procurement for potential reserved capacity pricing — I’ll bring a procurement lead if we get to contracting.\\n\\nCan you confirm the proposed kickoff dates (week of July 12) and whether you can support a quick POC with regional nodes in us-west-2?\\n\\n— Jacob\\nDirector of AI Engineering, ClearWell Health\\njacob@clearwellhealth.com\\n', 'From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>\\nTo: Jacob Lee <jacob@clearwellhealth.com>\\nCc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>\\nDate: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule\\n\\nJacob —\\n\\nGreat questions. Short answers up front: yes to us-west-2 nodes for the POC; yes we can keep POC data de-identified; and we can propose a Dedicated pool sized for 1–2k qps with a test harness to reproduce your burst patterns.\\n\\nRegarding a factual noisy-neighbor timeline: see Vanessa’s note below for a sanitized timeline and the mitigation steps we used (isolated tenant, scaled pool, temporary fallback to smaller model). We redact customer-identifying fields but keep the event timing and operational steps.\\n\\nI attached the playbook which includes a short case study (page 6) that mirrors the incident type you asked about. The poa_slo_table.xlsx shows recommended p95/p99 targets across modes. If those numbers look reasonable, I’ll ask Solutions to size the Dedicated PoC and send a scope doc.\\n\\nProposed POC: 2 weeks, Dedicated pool in us-west-2, VPC peering, synthetic load that mimics your spike profile, plus 48-hour soak. Proposed kickoff: July 12, wrap July 23.\\n\\nCan you confirm: 1) de-id dataset ready for July 12? 2) anyone from your networking team to approve peering?\\n\\nThanks — I’ll hold July 12 tentative and get Vanessa to add her technical detail.\\n\\nBest,\\nMichael\\n\\nAttachment: redwood-tenancy-playbook.pdf\\n', 'From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>\\nTo: Jacob Lee <jacob@clearwellhealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:07:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule\\n\\nHi Jacob —\\n\\nBelow is a concise, sanitized timeline of a noisy-neighbor incident we can share during the call. I’ve kept it short and operational. See attached poa_slo_table.xlsx for exact numbers we tracked.\\n\\n- T0 (09:05): Sudden surge from tenant A due to bulk async exports; sustained CPU/GPU queue growth observed.\\n- T0+4m: p99 token latency increased from ~420ms to ~1.6s on shared pool. System alerted via tracing and tail-latency monitors.\\n- T0+12m: Automated routing policy kicked in — new requests routed to standby Dedicated-compatible nodes; existing long-running requests continued on original nodes.\\n- T0+18m: Ops scaled Dedicated pool for tenant A (manual bump + autoscale triggers adjusted).\\n- T0+30m: Performance returned to baseline for foreground traffic; background batch jobs rethrottled.\\n- Root cause: large off-hours export that pinned GPU resources and increased KV cache churn; unexpected batching patterns aggravated the tail.\\n\\nMitigations we use that help ClearWell use case:\\n- Prefetching and cache partitioning for heavy KV workloads.\\n- Request routing policies that divert riskier, batchy requests to isolated capacity.\\n- Real-time tail-latency alarms with automated circuit-breaker style fallbacks (downgrade model or route to lower-cost variant) to protect p99.\\n\\nFor the POC we recommend:\\n1) Dedicated pool with an autoscale floor sized for your 1–2k qps baseline and headroom for bursts.\\n2) VPC peering to keep traffic inside your network boundary.\\n3) A short runbook step to exercise the routing fallback during the test so you can see the behavior end-to-end.\\n\\nAttachment: poa_slo_table.xlsx (sample p95/p99 by model + mode)\\n\\nHappy to jump on a tech session to walk the playbook and the POC runbook.\\n\\n— Vanessa Ortiz\\nSenior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference\\nvanessa@redwood.com\\n', 'From: Jacob Lee <jacob@clearwellhealth.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 14:45:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Isolation evidence, SLO examples, and proposed POC schedule\\n\\nThanks Vanessa — that timeline is exactly what we needed to see. A couple of final asks before we lock dates: \\n\\n- Procurement will need an outline of reserved-capacity pricing and the minimum commit for the Dedicated option. Can you send a ballpark number we can use internally?\\n- We’ll run the de-id dataset and confirm by EOD Monday (July 5).\\n- For SOC 2 / compliance artifacts: do you have an SOC 2 letter or SOC 2 audit contact we can talk to? We may need to include that prior to procurement approval.\\n\\nAssuming numbers look reasonable, we’re good to proceed with the July 12 kickoff for the POC. Please send pricing and the SOC 2 contact.\\n\\n— Jacob\\n\\n', '']
